correctness.rationale: The conditional record probability is 1/i when j>i, 1/(i-1) when j<i, and binom(n-1,i-1)^(-1) when j=i. Multiplication by P(I_j)=1/n and subtraction of 1/(ni) proves the entire matrix. Row summation gives reciprocal-binomial covariances, while binomial monotonicity and classical exact variances establish signs and asymptotics. Full enumeration n=2..8 and exact algebraic tests n=2..99 passed 324079 assertions. Finite checks are not used as universal proof.

value.rationale: The joint record/fixed-point dependence matrix is a natural structural invariant of uniform shuffles: conditioning on a fixed point before, at or after a record position creates a sharp lower-triangular support and a diagonal sign reversal. The nontrivial cancellation into reciprocal binomial row sums and the sharp O(1/(n sqrt(log n))) correlation yield a quantitative baseline for combining two classical permutation diagnostics, not obtainable from their marginal distributions.
